name: Roland JV-1080
source: Roland JV-1080 Owner's Manual (1994; MIDI Implementation 'Version 1.00, July 9 1994', pp.130-155; waveform list pp.122-123; parameter chapters pp.44-72; EFX pp.84-99, 114-120), https://static.roland.com/assets/media/pdf/JV-1080_OM.pdf (scanned; read from 300 dpi page renders). Cross-checked: Roland JV-1010 Owner's Manual MIDI Implementation (https://static.roland.com/assets/media/pdf/JV-1010_OM.pdf; same patch-tone map, wave group IDs, and the EFX Parameter 1-12 slot map); audiocontrol-org/audiocontrol modules/sampler-devices/src/devices/jv1080 (header, checksum, system offsets, EFX type names only); Edisyn RolandJV880 (eclab/edisyn) for the JV-family request/dump pattern (JV-880 = model 46H, different map). Note: Roland's current 'JV-1080_Manual_eng02_W.pdf' is the Roland Cloud plug-in manual, not the hardware.

roland.checksum: Sum every byte after the command byte and before the checksum (the 4 address bytes plus all data bytes for DT1, or the 4 address + 4 size bytes for RQ1); checksum = (128 - (sum % 128)) % 128, i.e. the 7 low bits of address+data+checksum total 0. Manual examples: F0 41 10 6A 12 01 00 00 28 06 [51] F7; F0 41 10 6A 11 03 00 00 39 00 00 00 01 [43] F7; F0 41 10 6A 11 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 28 [58] F7.

messageFormat.RQ1: F0 41 <dev> 6A 11 <a1 a2 a3 a4> <s1 s2 s3 s4> <sum> F7 -- the JV answers with one or more DT1s containing only the valid data inside the requested range

roland.addressing: Addresses and sizes are 7-bit per byte (each byte 00-7F, carry at 128). Param address = block base + offset, where 'offset' in params is a linear byte index inside the block: address = base + [0, 0, offset >> 7, offset & 0x7F] with 7-bit carry. Only the tone blocks exceed 127 bytes: tone offset 128 (Reverb Send Level) is 7-bit '01 00', so tone 1's last byte is 03 00 11 00. Sizes are encoded the same way (129 = 00 00 01 01). In a DT1 carrying several bytes, data[i] is at linear offset start+i.

system.desc: system common (global). Not part of a patch; exclude from patch send/randomize. Panel mode lives here.

common.desc: patch-mode temporary patch (edit buffer): patch common

requests.editBuffer: Five RQ1s, one per block, each answered by one DT1: common F0 41 10 6A 11 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 48 35 F7 (72 bytes); tone t: address 03 00 (0E + 2t) 00, size 00 00 01 01 (129 bytes) -- tone1 F0 41 10 6A 11 03 00 10 00 00 00 01 01 6B F7, tone2 ... 03 00 12 00 00 00 01 01 69 F7, tone3 ... 03 00 14 00 00 00 01 01 67 F7, tone4 ... 03 00 16 00 00 00 01 01 65 F7. Alternative (unverified): one RQ1 at 03 00 00 00 with size 00 00 17 01 should return the same five DT1s.
requests.forcePatchMode: F0 41 10 6A 12 00 00 00 00 01 7F F7 (System Panel Mode = PATCH). Give it ~200 ms before the next request (Edisyn uses 200 ms on the JV-880).

roland.userPatch: User patch n (1-128) = base [0x11, n-1, 0x00, 0x00]; same internal layout as the temporary patch: common at [0x11, n-1, 0x00, 0x00] (72 bytes), tone t at [0x11, n-1, 0x10 + 2*(t-1), 0x00] (129 bytes). Manual example (tone 2 of USER:02): F0 41 10 6A 11 11 01 12 00 00 00 01 01 5A F7. Backup = RQ1 each block (5 per patch) and keep the DT1 replies. Write = send the 5 DT1s to the user address (common + 4 tones, 20+ ms apart); a DT1 to user memory writes directly (no separate WRITE step) and is refused while UTILITY > PROTECT > Exclusive Protect is ON. Card patches: [0x21, n-1, ...] (only with a DATA card in the slot). Preset/expansion patches have no address -- load them via Bank Select + PC, then read the temporary area. Other user areas: performances 10 00..10 1F, rhythm sets 10 40/10 41.
roland.notes: SOUND MODE: the JV is always in PERFORMANCE, PATCH or GM panel mode (System 00 00 00 00 = 0/1/2). The temporary patch at 03 00 00 00 is what sounds in PATCH mode; in PERFORMANCE mode each part has its own temporary patch at 02 pp 00 00 (part 10 = rhythm setup 02 09 00 00), so edits to 03 are not heard. Force PATCH mode with the forcePatchMode DT1 before editing or requesting. In PATCH mode the unit listens on Patch Receive Channel (System 00 1D) for notes/PC/bank select. RX/TX: the unit only accepts SysEx when SYSTEM > SYS-EXC MIDI Rx.Exc = ON, and only if the message Device ID = Unit # - 1 (Unit # 17-32 -> 0x10-0x1F; default 17 = 0x10). Tx.Exc = ON makes the JV transmit a DT1 for every front-panel edit of a patch/rhythm parameter (useful for decode). The JV-1080 never sends RQ1 and does not do handshake transfers (one-way only). LIMITS: a DT1 carries at most 256 data bytes (Roland rule); the largest JV block is 129, so one DT1 per block. Leave more than 20 ms between successive DT1/RQ1 messages (manual p.131). Wave Number and Default Tempo are 2-byte nibbled values and should be written in one DT1 (address of the first byte, 2 data bytes). Messages whose address/size fall outside the map are ignored (front panel shows 'Exclusive Address Error'); bad checksums show 'Check Sum Error'. A DT1 with Wave Number above the group's wave count, or Velocity Range Lower > Upper, is ignored. TEMPORARY vs USER: temporary = volatile edit buffer (lost on patch change or power off); user = battery-backed memory, written directly by DT1 (see userPatch). Changing patch (PC / bank select / panel) overwrites the temporary area. FIRMWARE: the MIDI Implementation is 'Version 1.00, July 9 1994'; no later map revisions are known. The later JV-2080/JV-1010 keep this tone map byte-for-byte.

encodings.nibble: 2 bytes, 4 bits each, most-significant nibble first: value = (b0 << 4) | b1; write [value >> 4, value & 0x0F]. Manual: 'data ABH is divided into 0AH and 0BH and sent in that order'.
encodings.bipolar: stored offset-binary; display = value + valueOffset (e.g. 0-126 with valueOffset -63 -> -63..+63).

roland.userPatchNote: user patch n (0-127): replace the temporary block's first two address bytes (03 00) with (11, n) — common 11 n 00 00, tone t 11 n (10+2(t-1)) 00. Verified on hardware 2026-09-30 (patch 1 'CFC Ganymede', patch 128 'CFC Groundlp').

waves.note: Internal waveform names from the Owner's Manual pp.122-123. waves[group][waveNumber] where waveNumber is the stored 0-based value (display = value+1). Group selection: Wave Group 0 (INT) + Wave Group ID 1 = INT-A (255 waves), ID 2 = INT-B (193 waves). PCM (group 1) and EXP (group 2) names are not listed; EXP Group ID = SR-JV80 board number (see uncertain). 'type' L = loop, O = one-shot is in the manual but omitted here.

efxTypesNote: EFX Parameter n (common offset 0x0C + n) meaning per EFX Type, with the raw value range for that slot. Slot order is from the JV-1010 manual's 'Correspondence of the EFX algorithm and Exclusive Address (EFX Parameter 1-12)' table (same 40-type EFX); the JV-1080 manual lists the same parameters in display order, which differs from slot order (e.g. OVERDRIVE displays Drive/Level/LowGain/HiGain/Amp/Pan but slots are Drive/Pan/Amp/Low/High/Level). Slots past the listed params are unused. Raw -> display: Gain 0-30 = -15..+15 dB; Pan 0-127 = L64..63R; Balance 0-100 = D100:0E..D0:100E; Phase 0-90 = 0..180 deg; Feedback 0-98 = -98..+98 %; HF Damp 0-17 = 200..8000 Hz/BYPASS; Peak Freq / Cutoff 0-16 = 200..8000 Hz; Q 0-4 = 0.5/1.0/2.0/4.0/9.0; Rate/Pre Delay/Delay 0-125/126 are non-linear (Hz / ms tables in the JV-1080 manual pp.84-99, not modelled).

programs.note: PATCH mode, on the Patch Receive Channel: CC0 = msb, CC32 = lsb, then Program Change 0-127 (manual p.133). Bank select is only latched and takes effect on the next PC; System 'Receive Bank Select' and 'Receive Program Change' must be ON. Expansion banks exist only when that SR-JV80 board is fitted (many boards have fewer than 256 patches); card banks only with a card inserted. Only 'user' is writable over SysEx (see roland.userPatch); read any bank by selecting it and requesting the temporary patch. Performance mode uses a different table (MSB 80/81/82 + PC 0-31).

setup: Press [PATCH] so the JV is in Patch mode (not Performance, not GM). The editor can also force it with a DT1 to 00 00 00 00 = 1, but not reliably out of GM mode.
[SYSTEM] > SYS-EXC MIDI: Unit # = 17 (Device ID 16 / 0x10, the editor default), Rx.Exc = ON, Tx.Exc = ON (front-panel edits come back as DT1).
[SYSTEM] > Patch Receive Channel = the channel picked above.
[SYSTEM] > Rx MIDI: Receive Program Change = ON, Receive Bank Select = ON.
[UTILITY] > PROTECT: Exclusive Protect = OFF (needed only to write user patches; it resets to OFF at power-on).
Cable both ways: interface out -> JV MIDI IN, JV MIDI OUT -> interface in (RQ1 replies need the return path).
uncertain: Velocity sensitivities (P-Env, Resonance, F-Env, A-Env) 0-125: the JV-1080 MIDI implementation prints '(-50 - +200)', but the same manual's parameter lists (pp.53-56, 64-65) say -100 to +150 and the JV-1080-compatible JV-1010 map says -100-+150. Options use -100..+150 in steps of 2 (value*2-100). The printed -50..+200 looks like a typo; not verified on hardware.
P-Env Time 4 is printed at offset '00 48' (duplicating Time 3). 0x49 is used: the sequence 46-4D requires it and the JV-1010 map prints 00 49.

Tone Delay Mode value 2 is 'KEY-INTERVAL' in the MIDI implementation and 'PLAY-MATE' on the panel (p.50); labelled PLAYMATE. The JV-1010 adds an 8th value TEMPO-SYNC which the JV-1080 does not list; the range is kept at 0-6.

Wave Group ID values (INT-A = 1, INT-B = 2) are not stated in the JV-1080 manual; they come from the JV-1010 manual (same internal waves). PCM group ID = card ID and EXP group ID = SR-JV80 board number (JV-1010 lists 'Session' = 9; an Electra One user reports EXP groupId 0x0A for a board and 3 for PCM card no.5). Verify by reading a patch that uses each board.

EFX Parameter 1-12 slot meanings (efxTypes) come from the JV-1010 manual, not the JV-1080 manual (which only gives display order). The parameter sets match type-for-type, so this is very likely correct, but it is not verified on a JV-1080. REVERB slot 3 is printed 'Gate Time' in the JV-1010 table; named 'Reverb Time' here from the JV-1080 parameter list.

Single-message whole-patch RQ1 (03 00 00 00, size 00 00 17 01) follows Roland's rule that the reply contains only valid data in the range, and Edisyn does the same on the JV-880. Not verified on the JV-1080; the five-RQ1 form is the documented safe path.
Pan LFO depth 0-126 is printed '(L63 - 63R)'; treated as bipolar -63..+63. Alternate Pan Depth 1-127 '(L63 - 63R)' is treated as valueOffset -64 (64 = centre).

System 'Patch mode patch group / group ID / number' (00 00 00 02-05) could select a patch over SysEx, but the manual only lists groups USER/PCM/EXP without group-ID meanings (the JV-1010 uses USER = 0/1, PR-A..= 0/3..). Use Bank Select + PC instead.
Performance Number (system 00 01) mapping of 0-127 to USER/CARD/PR-A/PR-B 1-32 is assumed to be 32 per group in that order.
Master Tune 0-126 = 427.4-452.6 Hz is assumed linear at 0.2 Hz per step (63 = 440.0).
Getting out of GM mode over SysEx reportedly does not work (Electra One forum). Switch to Patch mode on the front panel first.

An Electra One user reports 'Receive Data Error' when sending Wave Number for an SR-JV80-03 board (also with MidiQuest). Possibly a board with fewer waves than the value sent; be careful with EXP wave numbers.

No per-message or per-knob throttle is documented beyond 'more than 20 ms between DT1 messages' (written for bulk transfers). Continuous knob sweeps faster than that are common practice on Roland units but not guaranteed.

Note display: key-range/bias values are MIDI note numbers with 0 = C-1 and 60 = C4 (Roland labels C-1..G9). The rack editor's 'note' formatter prints octave floor(v/12), i.e. C0 for 0; it needs a -1 octave for this device.

Display offset field: this schema uses 'valueOffset' (because 'offset' is the byte offset). The current editor.js fmt() reads p.offset for display, so it would add the byte offset to the shown value until it is changed to valueOffset for roland schemas.

Wave list transcription: two names are kept exactly as printed although they look like typos: INT-B 159 'REV DrySick' (DryStick) and 164 'REV Clve'. INT-A has 'MonoStringsA'/'MonoStringsC' with no B, and 'French 1A'/'French 1C' with no B, as printed.
Expansion bank patch counts: the table allows 1-256 per slot, but most SR-JV80 boards hold 255 patches or fewer. Sending a PC past the last patch is untested.
